bioengineering.overview: Explore how engineering and life science come together to develop and evaluate systems and products connected to health.
activities: Design or evaluate devices and systems connected to health.
Use engineering and biological knowledge to investigate a problem.
bioengineering.mission: Sketch a fictional device that could make an everyday task easier. Label one question you would need to investigate. Do not test medical devices or give health advice.

source.title: Software Developers, Quality Assurance Analysts, and Testers

software.overview: Explore how people design, build and test applications that help someone do a task.
activities: Ask what users need and design software around those needs.
Test an application and document problems or improvements.
software.mission: Draw three screens for a tiny app that helps with a fictional everyday task. Write one test you would try.

source.title: Web Developers and Digital Designers
source.source: BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook — related digital-interface work

design.overview: Explore the look, layout and usability of digital interfaces. This world connects to digital-interface design; it is not a claim that every product-design role has the same requirements.
activities: Create a prototype or mockup of an interface.
Test layouts and navigation to see how an interface works for a user.
design.mission: Sketch two versions of a fictional app screen. Explain which version makes its main action easier to find.

environment.overview: Explore how scientists investigate environmental questions, study data and communicate possible solutions.
activities: Prepare reports or presentations explaining research findings.
environment.mission: Choose a safe observation such as counting reusable bottles in a fictional classroom. Make a sample table and list one question the data could help explore.
